title.narrative: Goat milk value chain in Samburu central sub-county, Samburu county, Kenya.

description.narrative: The county government of Samburu and other development partners including Caritas Maralal have been putting efforts to support women and youth improve milk production and fight poverty through support ranging from goat provision (local and improved breeds) and capacity building initiatives like trainings. However, there still is a huge gap in joint collaboration from stakeholders in strengthening the goat milk value chain. In a recent market system analysis on goat milk value chain carried out by CAFOD through Fair and sustainable consulting, there exists a large gap between goat milk production and demand mainly because production is at subsistence level rather than commercial. Goat farming in Samburu County is mostly carried out by women and youth to provide alternative income for household consumption and other expenditures. Dairy goats can bear offspring twice an year, with one goat producing at least 1 litre of milk per day. As per the analysis carried out by CAFOD through Fair and Sustainable Consulting, Samburu central has a ready market for milk and the demand is currently higher than production. There is a conducive environment for production and favourable climatic condition to support goat farming and goat milk production and their feeds. This project proposes a number of activities to address issues hindering expansion and commercialization of goat milk among indigenous pastoralist women and youth. The issues to be addressed include lack of coordination among key actors in the goat milk value chain, low production of milk from both local and dairy goats, a lack of linkage among goat farmers themselves and a lack of strong policy environment to support the value chain. The target location for this project is Samburu central with the main target being youth and women. The project will reach estimated 3340 farmers(2380f,960m)
